title: Compiled queries
description: Learn how EF Core compiled queries cache LINQ-to-SQL translation plans to reduce overhead on frequently executed queries.

data.text: Every time EF Core encounters a new LINQ query shape, it must translate the expression tree into SQL, cache the translation plan, and build a query pipeline. For queries that run thousands of times per second — such as lookups by ID — this translation overhead adds up. Compiled queries let you pre-compile and cache the translation so EF Core skips the planning phase.

A compiled query is an `EF.CompileQuery` delegate that wraps a LINQ expression. The first time the delegate runs, EF Core translates the expression into SQL and caches the plan. Subsequent executions with different parameter values reuse the cached plan, saving the translation cost. The speedup is most noticeable on hot paths that execute the same query pattern repeatedly.

data.title: Defining and using a compiled query

data.text: EF Core 7+ supports async compiled queries with `EF.CompileAsyncQuery`. These return `Task<T>` results and work with async database providers. Use async compiled queries when your data access is already asynchronous to avoid blocking threads on the execution path.

data.title: Async compiled query

items: Queries that return a single entity or scalar value using FirstOrDefault, SingleOrDefault, or Count.
Queries that return lists with ToList or ToArray.
Queries with multiple parameters, as long as the expression shape stays the same.
Queries that include related data via Include.

data.title: Query shape must be static
data.text: Compiled queries cache the expression tree structure. You cannot conditionally add or remove Include, Where, or OrderBy clauses inside a compiled query. If the shape changes, EF Core falls back to normal query execution and logs a warning.

Compiled queries shine in high-throughput scenarios: API endpoints that run the same lookup repeatedly, background services processing messages in a loop, or real-time applications with tight latency budgets. For infrequent or one-off queries, the overhead of compiling is not worth the saved translation time.

data.title: Compiled query in a background service

items: Compiled queries must be defined as static delegates — they cannot capture local variables.
They are not compatible with all query patterns, such as ExecuteUpdate or ExecuteDelete in EF Core 7+.
The performance benefit is proportional to how often the same query shape is reused.
Overusing compiled queries for every query in a large codebase adds maintenance complexity without proportional gains.

data.title: Key takeaways
items: Compiled queries cache the LINQ-to-SQL translation plan for repeated reuse.
Use EF.CompileQuery for synchronous and EF.CompileAsyncQuery for async execution.
Best suited for hot paths: frequent lookups, background processing, real-time APIs.
Keep the query shape static — dynamic Include or Where logic breaks compilation.
